name: Turkmenistan
snapshot: One of the world's most closed countries, sitting on huge gas reserves, where the former president handed power to his son and still rules alongside him.
leader: The Berdimuhamedov family (Gurbanguly, then his son Serdar)
culture: Turkmen culture prizes the Akhal-Teke horse, a national symbol with its own holiday, and hand-woven carpets, which appear on the flag. The capital, Ashgabat, has built endless white marble monuments and gilded statues. The Darvaza gas crater, nicknamed the "Gates of Hell", has burned since 1971.
society: Turkmenistan has the world's fourth-largest gas reserves, sold mostly to China. Information is tightly controlled, the internet heavily censored and foreign travel restricted. Shortages and hidden inflation have driven emigration, mainly to Turkey.
situation: Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov handed the presidency to his son Serdar in 2022 but remains "National Leader" and chairman of the upper house of parliament, and is widely seen as the real power. There are no independent parties or media.
power: A presidential republic in form and a personalist autocracy in practice. The People's Council, chaired by the former president, sits above parliament, and no opposition is allowed.

leaders.gov: Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov, National Leader and chairman of the People's Council
